unsigned_reason: The board signer runs as OIDC inside GitHub Actions, disabled account-wide.
what_this_measures: Every .ots under public/ was parsed with the official opentimestamps Python library, its attestations classified BY TYPE, and every BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation checked against real block headers fetched from three independent public sources. A proof is called BITCOIN_VERIFIED only where the merkle root the proof derives equals the merkle root in the real block header at the claimed height, with at least two independent sources agreeing on that header. A parsed Bitcoin attestation that was not checked against a block is not a verified proof.

method.enumeration: os.walk over public/, every file ending .ots, tracked and untracked alike
method.merkle_extraction: Timestamp.all_attestations() yields (msg, attestation). For a BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation the msg IS the digest the proof commits to, i.e. the block's merkle root in internal byte order; it is byte-reversed for display comparison.
method.agreement_rule: at least two independent sources must return the same merkle_root for the height
method.unreachable_rule: fewer than two reachable sources => BITCOIN_CLAIMED_UNVERIFIED, never BITCOIN_VERIFIED
method.digest_binding_rule: the proof's file_digest is recomputed from the sibling file with the proof's own file_hash_op
method.read_only: no .ots file in the repository was written, repaired or upgraded

control_a.description: one byte flipped in the merkle root the proof derives; same predicate re-run

control_b.description: end-to-end: a single byte flipped inside the merkle path of a scratchpad COPY, then the full pipeline re-run against the real chain header

findings: 56 of 594 .ots files under public/ carry a BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation and every one of them verified against the real chain: the merkle root each proof derives equals the merkle root in the block header at the claimed height. 104 of 104 block heights verified, none failed.

Only 10 of those 56 Bitcoin-anchored proofs can be shown to bind to a file in this tree. For the other 46 the file the proof timestamps is NOT present in the repository (the root-<hex>.json payloads were never committed), so the anchor is real but what it anchors cannot be checked here. Anchored is not the same as bound.
536 .ots files are PENDING: calendar commitments only, no Bitcoin attestation. Today's ~490 new stamps are in this group and are correctly labelled PENDING_CALENDAR_COMMITMENT.

2 proofs DO NOT BIND to the file they sit beside. They are not the same defect: door-demand-payai-2026-09-17.json.ots still binds to the COMMITTED bytes at HEAD and was broken only by an uncommitted working-tree edit made 30 minutes after stamping; mirror-manifest.json.ots binds to bytes that exist nowhere, because its target is untracked and regenerated — it changed digest twice during this run. See mismatch_forensics on each artifact.
Three independent chain sources agreed on all 104 block headers. No disagreement.

The failing control fired: a single flipped byte in the derived merkle root, and a single flipped byte inside the merkle path of a scratchpad copy of a real proof, were both REJECTED by the same predicate that passed the genuine proofs.

Not one Bitcoin attestation failed its chain check. The 216 attestation instances across 104 heights all matched exactly, which is the expected outcome for genuine proofs and is not achievable by chance.
method_limitations: Block headers were read from three public HTTP APIs, not from a locally validated full node. Two-of-three agreement is corroboration, not independent consensus validation; all three could in principle be fed by a common upstream.
Proof-of-work on the returned headers was not independently checked, and no check was made that the claimed height is on the most-work chain beyond what the APIs report as main chain.

A verified merkle root proves the digest was committed to that block. It does not prove who created the digest, nor that the digest's preimage is the file you think it is; that is what the separate digest_binding check is for.
For 46 proofs the timestamped file is absent from this tree, so digest binding is UNTESTED, not passing.
Only public/ was scanned, in the working tree at git HEAD 2a440d2e2294, including untracked files present on disk at the time of the run.
Block times are the header nTime as reported by the sources; Bitcoin timestamps are bounded, not exact wall-clock.
This artifact is unsigned. The board signer runs as OIDC inside GitHub Actions, disabled account-wide.

The working tree was dirty and contained regenerating untracked files during the run; two digest comparisons were made against bytes that changed under the reader. Both cases are recorded in mismatch_forensics rather than smoothed over.

mismatch_forensics.reading: The proof DOES bind to the committed bytes at HEAD. The working tree copy was edited at 13:27Z, after the proof was written at 12:57Z, and is uncommitted. The proof is sound against what is published; the local edit is not yet published. If that edit is committed as-is the published file will stop matching its own proof.
mismatch_forensics.action: do not commit the working-tree edit without re-stamping

mismatch_forensics.reading: The target is untracked and is being regenerated locally: its digest changed twice during this single verification run (mtime 14:37Z, proof written 13:37Z), and no commit in its history carries the digest the proof expects. This proof binds to bytes that no longer exist anywhere. It is a proof of nothing that is still on disk.
mismatch_forensics.action: this .ots must not be published; stamp a frozen artifact, not a regenerated one
